intent: To inform viewers that cat owners are more likely to be introverted.

units.meaning: Cat owners are more likely to be introverted than a reference/comparison group.

basis.note: Table row encodes a positive comparative likelihood; baseline group is not specified in the table. Subject 'cat owners' comes from intent/narration.

accepted_routes: Cat owners are more likely to be introverted.
Cat people tend to be more introverted.
People who own cats have a higher likelihood of introversion.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A comparison cue must show cat owners as higher/more likely on introversion, not lower or equal.
units.temporal_anchor: The main clause 'more likely to be introverted' should carry this direction.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show or state the comparison direction rather than only displaying an 11% number?

units.meaning: The size of the relative likelihood difference is 11%, or 0.11 as a decimal.

basis.note: Table value is 11 with unit percent.

units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must display the 11% value or its 0.11 decimal equivalent as the magnitude of the effect.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration clause '11% more likely' should carry this magnitude.
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact 11%/0.11 magnitude appear, or is an approximate or rounded magnitude acceptable?

optional_valid: The single data point can be rendered as a donut/percent graphic rather than a bar chart.
The source type is printed, so the video may cite it as a printed statistic.
unsupported_to_avoid: Cat owners are 11 percentage points more introverted than non-cat owners.
Cat owners are more introverted than dog owners.
Any named comparison baseline, such as non-cat owners or dog owners, unless supplied by broader context.
notes: Only one table row exists, so the main trade-off is whether the 11% is the required quantitative payload or only supports the qualitative direction. The table does not specify the comparison baseline, so any named baseline must be treated as unsupported unless supplied by broader context.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
